string.name: wizard_percentage_and_correction
string.comment: Bolus wizard result, shown after the amounts when both are changed. %1$s=percentage, %2$s=correction with its sign and unit. Example: 71% +1.00 U

string.name: wizard_calc_with_isf
string.comment: Line of the bolus wizard calculation. %1$s=what the insulin is for, %2$s=insulin sensitivity factor used. Example: BG (ISF: 3.0)

string.name: wizard_calc_with_ic
string.comment: Line of the bolus wizard calculation. %1$s=what the insulin is for, %2$s=insulin to carb ratio used. Example: COB (IC: 10.0)

string.name: wizard_calc_carbs_with_ic
string.comment: Line of the bolus wizard calculation for the carbs eaten now. %1$s=Carbs, %2$s=amount with unit, %3$s=insulin to carb ratio used. Example: Carbs 20 g (IC: 10.0)

string.name: wizard_carbs_type_desc
string.comment: What the cake or pizza carb type does. %1$d=percent the carbs are reduced by, %2$d=percent added as eCarbs, %3$d=minutes until the eCarbs start, %4$d=hours they are spread over. Example: Carbs reduced by 10%, added eCarbs 20% delayed 60 min for 2 h

resources.string: Carbs reduced by %1$d%%, added eCarbs %2$d%% delayed %3$d min for %4$d h

Tap to include/exclude from calculation:
• BG — blood glucose (ON at start)
• TT — temp target (ON at start)
• Trend — BG trend (last state remembered)
• IOB — insulin on board (ON at start)
• COB — carbs on board (last state remembered)

string.name: a11y_bg_graph_summary
string.comment: Screen-reader description of the glucose graph, which is drawn and so cannot be read otherwise. %1$s=the recent glucose values newest first, already joined and carrying their unit, %2$s=insulin on board with its label, %3$s=carbs on board with its label. Example: Glucose graph. Recent values 7.2, 7.0, 6.8. IOB: 1.20 U. COB: 45 g

string.name: a11y_show_controls
string.comment: Screen-reader name of the invisible area that brings back the top bar, menu and toolbar on a short screen, where they hide by themselves.

string.name: a11y_notifications
string.comment: Screen-reader name of the notification button on the main screen. %1$d=number of notifications. Example: Notifications: 3

string.name: a11y_tt_none
string.comment: Screen-reader state of the temp target chip when no temp target is running; the chip then shows the profile target.

string.name: a11y_tt_adjusted
string.comment: Screen-reader state of the temp target chip when the loop has changed the target; on screen this is only a colour.

string.name: a11y_profile_entry
string.comment: Screen-reader name of one value field in the profile editor. %1$s=the list it belongs to, with its unit (e.g. Basal [U/h]), %2$s=the start time of that entry. Example: Basal [U/h] at 08:00

string.name: a11y_bg_delta
string.comment: Screen-reader text for the change since the previous glucose reading. %1$s=the change with its sign and unit. Example: delta +0.3

string.name: a11y_bg_old_reading
string.comment: Screen-reader word added to a glucose reading that is too old to trust. On screen the value is struck through.

string.name: a11y_bg_age_old
string.comment: Screen-reader text for the age of a glucose reading that is too old to trust. %1$s=the age, %2$s=a11y_bg_old_reading. Example: (12 min), old reading

string.name: a11y_bg_graph_summary_values_only
string.comment: Same as a11y_bg_graph_summary but for the history browser, where insulin and carbs on board are current values and would be wrong beside a past day. %1$s=the glucose values newest first, already joined and carrying their unit.

string.name: a11y_predictions
string.comment: Screen-reader description of the predicted glucose curves, which are drawn on the graph and cannot be read otherwise. %1$s=one sentence per prediction, already joined. Example: Predictions. COB prediction rises to 11.2 mmol/l. IOB prediction falls to 4.8 mmol/l.

string.name: a11y_prediction_rises
string.comment: One predicted curve that ends higher than the current glucose. %1$s=the name of the prediction, %2$s=the highest value it reaches, with its unit. Example: COB prediction rises to 11.2 mmol/l

string.name: a11y_prediction_falls
string.comment: One predicted curve that ends lower than the current glucose. %1$s=the name of the prediction, %2$s=the lowest value it reaches, with its unit. Example: IOB prediction falls to 4.8 mmol/l

string.name: a11y_prediction_flat
string.comment: One predicted curve that stays level. %1$s=the name of the prediction, %2$s=the value it holds, with its unit. Example: Zero temp prediction stays at 6.1 mmol/l

string.name: a11y_prediction_name_iob
string.comment: Spoken name of the prediction from insulin on board. IOB is the term AAPS users know.

string.name: a11y_prediction_name_cob
string.comment: Spoken name of the prediction from carbs on board. COB is the term AAPS users know.

string.name: a11y_prediction_name_acob
string.comment: Spoken name of the prediction from already absorbed carbs, shown by the AMA algorithm only.

string.name: a11y_prediction_name_uam
string.comment: Spoken name of the prediction for a meal the user did not enter. UAM is the term AAPS users know.

string.name: a11y_prediction_name_zt
string.comment: Spoken name of the prediction for what happens with no insulin at all, the zero-temp curve.

string.name: a11y_badge_attention
string.comment: Screen-reader state of a navigation button that carries a warning badge. On screen the badge is a dot or an exclamation mark, which a screen reader cannot see at all.

string.name: a11y_badge_available
string.comment: Screen-reader state of a navigation button whose badge counts what the user can start right now. %1$d=the count. Example: 3 available

string.name: a11y_objectives_progress
string.comment: Screen-reader state of the Objectives navigation button, whose badge shows progress. %1$d=objectives finished, %2$d=objectives in total. Example: 9 of 10 done

string.name: execute_label
string.comment: Button that runs the selected quick wizard, which delivers its bolus.

string.name: stats_tab_cycle
string.comment: Short tab label on the Statistics screen. The tab shows daily insulin totals laid over 28-day cycles (TDD Cycle Pattern).

string.name: a11y_quick_launch_add
string.comment: Screen-reader label of the button that adds an action to the QuickLaunch bar. %1$s=the action name. Example: Add Bolus wizard

string.name: a11y_quick_launch_remove
string.comment: Screen-reader label of the button that removes an action from the QuickLaunch bar. %1$s=the action name. Example: Remove Bolus wizard

string.name: graph_therapy_event_bg_with_note

string.name: exercise_mode
string.comment: Name of the overview button that switches the autoISF exercise mode. In this mode a high temp target raises the insulin sensitivity.

string.name: exercise_mode_on
string.comment: Spoken state of the exercise mode button when the mode is on

string.name: exercise_mode_off
string.comment: Spoken state of the exercise mode button when the mode is off

string.name: basal_card
string.comment: Name of the overview card that shows the basal insulin rate given now

string.name: basal_unknown
string.comment: Shown instead of a rate or a percent that is not known

string.name: basal_percent_of_profile
string.comment: %1$d=the basal given now as percent of the basal of the active profile. Example: 150% of profile

string.name: basal_by_profile
string.comment: Short status: the pump gives the basal of the profile, no temp basal runs

string.name: basal_tbr_left
string.comment: Short status of a running temp basal (TBR). %1$d=minutes left. Example: TBR · 12 min left

string.name: basal_profile_switch_short
string.comment: Short status of an active profile switch (PS). %1$d=its percentage. Example: PS 110%

string.name: basal_requested_short
string.comment: Short status: the loop asked for a temp basal the pump has not set yet. %1$s=rate with unit. Example: Asked 0.90 U/h

string.name: basal_status_join
string.comment: Joins two short statuses of the basal card. %1$s and %2$s are statuses. Example: 150% of profile · TBR · 12 min left

string.name: basal_details_profile_switch_value
string.comment: %1$d=percentage, %2$d=time shift in hours. Example: 110%, time shift 2 h

string.name: basal_details_tbr_value
string.comment: %1$s=rate with unit, %2$d=minutes it runs in total. Example: 0.75 U/h for 30 min

string.name: basal_details_requested
string.comment: Label of a temp basal the loop asked for and the pump has not set yet

resources.string: Asked by the loop, not set yet

string.name: basal_details_pump_data
string.comment: State of the pump with the age of its newest data. %1$d=minutes. Example: Data 2 min old

Basal of the profile over the day

string.name: basal_inspect_with_profile
string.comment: Basal on the graph at the chosen time. %1$s=basal given with unit, %2$s=basal of the profile with unit. Example: 0.75 U/h (profile 0.50 U/h)

string.name: today_tir_short
string.comment: Short name of time in range on the overview statistics

string.name: today_cv_short
string.comment: Short name of the coefficient of variation of BG on the overview statistics

string.name: today_percent_whole
string.comment: %1$d=percent. Example: 51%

string.name: today_percent_one_decimal
string.comment: %1$.1f=percent with one decimal. Example: 39.5%

string.name: nav_history
string.comment: Bottom menu: opens the history browser. Keep it short.

string.name: graph_card_history
string.comment: Spoken name of the button that opens the history browser from the graph card

string.name: graph_range_hours
string.comment: Button that shows the last hours on the graph. %1$d=hours. Example: 6 h

string.name: graph_layer_predictions
string.comment: Switch of a graph layer, keep it short: the predictions of the loop

string.name: graph_layer_parabola
string.comment: Switch of a graph layer, keep it short: the BG parabola of autoISF

string.name: graph_layer_gru
string.comment: Switch of a graph layer, keep it short: the GRU model of the personal prediction. GRU is a name, do not translate

string.name: graph_layer_linear
string.comment: Switch of a graph layer, keep it short: the linear model of the personal prediction

string.name: graph_layer_activity
string.comment: Switch of a graph layer, keep it short: insulin activity, how fast insulin works now. Not physical exercise.

string.name: autoisf_factor_acce
string.comment: Key of a line in the AutoISF graph: the acceleration factor. Short, an algorithm term

string.name: autoisf_factor_bg
string.comment: Key of a line in the AutoISF graph: the BG factor. Short, an algorithm term

string.name: autoisf_factor_pp
string.comment: Key of a line in the AutoISF graph: the post-prandial factor. Short, an algorithm term

string.name: autoisf_factor_dura
string.comment: Key of a line in the AutoISF graph: the duration factor. Short, an algorithm term

string.name: autoisf_factor_final
string.comment: Key of a line in the AutoISF graph: the final factor. Short, an algorithm term

string.name: insulin_brand_preset
string.comment: Chip that loads the peak for an insulin by its trade name. %1$s=trade name, %2$s=peak with unit. Example: Fiasp (55 min)

string.name: graph_mini_map
string.comment: Spoken name of the small strip under the BG graph that shows the whole range

string.name: inspect_forecast
string.comment: Beside the time in the graph card when that time is after now, so the values there are a forecast

string.name: nav_treatments_log
string.comment: Bottom menu: opens the history of treatments (boluses, carbs, temp basals). Keep it short.

string.name: bolus_card
string.comment: Name of the overview card that shows the bolus advice and opens the bolus wizard

string.name: treatment_source_algorithm
string.comment: Treatment history: the bolus or temp basal was given by the loop

string.name: treatment_source_client
string.comment: Treatment history: given by a paired AAPSClient. %1$s=its device name. Example: Client: Pixel 7

string.name: treatment_source_client_or_ns
string.comment: Treatment history: given by a client whose name is not known, or entered in Nightscout

string.name: treatment_source_user
string.comment: Treatment history: given by the user of this phone

string.name: treatment_source_user_via
string.comment: Treatment history: given by the user of this phone, with the screen it came from. %1$s=screen. Example: You · Bolus wizard

string.name: bolus_rec_loop_gives
string.comment: %1$s=insulin with unit. Example: about 0.60 U

string.name: bolus_rec_carbs

string.name: bolus_rec_low_predicted

resources.string: Do not bolus: BG is predicted to go down to %1$s in the next 2 hours.

string.name: bolus_rec_in_one_hour
string.comment: %1$s=predicted BG with unit. Example: In 1 h: 6.2 mmol/l

string.name: bolus_rec_eventual
string.comment: %1$s=eventual BG of the loop with unit. Example: Eventual: 7.1 mmol/l

string.name: bolus_rec_needed
string.comment: %1$s=insulin with unit. Example: 0.40 U

string.name: bolus_rec_isf
string.comment: %1$s=BG with unit. Example: ISF: 3.0 mmol/l per U

string.name: bolus_rec_run_age
string.comment: %1$s=minutes with unit. Example: Loop run 3 min ago

string.name: bolus_rec_use
string.comment: Button that puts the advised dose into the amount field. %1$s=dose with unit. Example: Use 0.65 U

string.name: model_adv_title
string.comment: Title of the advice block of the personal prediction in the Insulin dialog

resources.string: No current prediction of the model.

string.name: model_adv_missing
string.comment: %1$s=insulin with unit. Example: About 0.65 U are missing.

string.name: model_adv_too_much
string.comment: %1$s=insulin with unit, %2$s=carbs with unit. Example: About 0.65 U too much insulin. About 8 g would cover it.

resources.string: About %1$s too much insulin. About %2$s would cover it.

string.name: model_adv_error

string.name: model_adv_trained
string.comment: %1$s=date and time

resources.string: The loop sets temp basals and SMBs by itself.
The loop suggests, you confirm every dose.
The loop only stops the basal when glucose is low.
Pick a mode to turn the loop on.
Basal follows the profile, no SMB. “No end” turns the loop off until you turn it on again.
For a shower or swimming: no insulin is given
The new time counts from now
